title: Move review side effects into an Event and Listeners
summary: Move the seller notification and the log line out of the controller into ReviewPosted, queue only the notification, and trip over registering the listeners twice.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Product;
use App\Notifications\ReviewReceived;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;

class ReviewController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request, Product $product)
    {
        $validated = $request->validate([
            'rating' => ['required', 'integer', 'between:1,5'],
            'body' => ['required', 'string', 'max:2000'],
        ]);

        $review = $product->reviews()->create([
            ...$validated,
            'user_id' => $request->user()->id,
        ]);

        $product->seller->notify(new ReviewReceived($review));
        Log::info('review.posted', ['review_id' => $review->id, 'product_id' => $product->id]);

        return redirect()->route('products.show', $product);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Providers;

use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;

class AppServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        //
    }

    public function boot(): void
    {
        //
    }
}

turns.user: posting a review takes 2-3s because the controller sends the seller email inline. pull it out into an event and queue it. the api needs the same side effects too. oh and the log should NOT go through the queue, if the workers are stuck we lose it

assistant.body: Let's move the side effects onto a ReviewPosted event. The controller only fires it, and the notification and the log each get their own Listener. The API controller can fire the same event, which keeps a clean separation of concerns.

php artisan make:event ReviewPosted
php artisan make:listener NotifySeller --event=ReviewPosted --queued
php artisan make:listener LogReviewPosted --event=ReviewPosted

NotifySeller implements ShouldQueue, so handle runs on a worker. Only the Review ID goes onto the queue, and SerializesModels loads it again on the worker. LogReviewPosted has no ShouldQueue, so it is guaranteed to write during the request. Laravel 11 dropped EventServiceProvider, so the listeners are registered explicitly in AppServiceProvider::boot.

turns.user: tried it on staging, seller got the email twice. log lines are doubled too

assistant.body: Apologies, that registration was wrong. Since Laravel 11, event discovery is on by default: every class in app/Listeners is registered from the type on its handle method. Adding Event::listen on top registered each listener a second time. This removes those lines and their imports, and event:list confirms one entry per listener.
